findings.title: Removing the BuildIndex lock lets concurrent builds for the same key race and leak indexes
findings.body: The mutex was removed from the whole of BuildIndex and now only guards the final `b.cache[key] = idx` write. Two callers can build the same namespace/resource at once, for example init() running while getOrCreateIndex is triggered by a Search or a watch event. For file-backed indexes both call `bleve.New(dir, mapper)` on the same directory, so one fails. For memory indexes both succeed, and the second cache write silently overwrites the first, which is never closed or flushed to disk. The original lock prevented this. Either restore per-key serialization (singleflight or a per-key mutex) or document that callers must never build the same key concurrently.

findings.title: TotalDocs iterates the cache map without holding cacheMu
findings.body: TotalDocs ranges over `b.cache` with no lock, while BuildIndex now writes `b.cache[key]` under `cacheMu.Lock()` and GetIndex reads it under RLock. The new `s.log.Info(... "total_docs", s.search.TotalDocs())` in searchSupport.init, and any other caller, can run concurrently with a background build from getOrCreateIndex or handleEvent. Go map read/write races can crash the process with 'concurrent map read and map write'. TotalDocs should take `cacheMu.RLock()`.

findings.title: Errgroup goroutines write to shared outer variables err and totalBatchesIndexed
findings.body: Inside the `group.Go` closure, `_, _, err = s.build(...)` assigns to the `err` declared in init(), and `totalBatchesIndexed++` mutates a shared int. Several goroutines run in parallel (SetLimit(initWorkers)), so this is a data race. A build error can also be overwritten or lost, and the value of `err` read after `group.Wait()` is not the error from the goroutine. The closure should declare its own local `err`, and the counter should be an atomic or be computed after Wait.

findings.title: Startup now fails hard if lifecycle init or the full index build fails
findings.body: Previously a failed Init was recorded in initErr and only surfaced on later RPCs, so the server still started. Now NewResourceServer returns an error when lifecycle.Init or search.init fails, and search.init blocks construction until every namespace is indexed. This changes module startup ordering and failure behaviour, and it runs lifecycle hooks (e.g. DB init) at construction time rather than on first use. Callers that construct the server before the database or other dependencies are ready can now fail at startup. This needs to be checked against the module wiring. Also, on this error path the `cancel` for the context created above is never called, so the background context leaks.

findings.title: GetResourceStats never closes the rows result set
findings.body: In the WithTx closure, `rows, err := dbutil.QueryRows(...)` is iterated but `rows.Close()` is never called, and `rows.Err()` is never checked. The function was modified in this PR, and the leak holds a DB connection/transaction resource until the transaction ends. Errors encountered during iteration are silently dropped, which can produce partial stats and a wrong index build. Add `defer rows.Close()` and check `rows.Err()`.

findings.title: Postgres variant of the storage-server test is silently skipped
findings.body: The new early return skips the test entirely for postgres with a comment that it is broken in CI. This hides any regression in the storage server startup path that this PR changes (the Init move into the constructor) for postgres runs, with no tracking issue referenced. The change is also unrelated to the stated PR scope.
